title: Trump Is Giving D.C. a Makeover — From a Blue Pool to a Giant Arch
summary: Have you ever wanted to redecorate your whole house? President Trump is doing that to Washington, D.C.! He's a real estate developer who says construction is "relaxation" for him. And he has big plans. First, the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — that long, shallow pool where people march and give speeches — is getting a new coat. Not just any color: Trump picked "American flag blue." He said a pool builder friend talked him out of a turquoise shade "like in the Bahamas." The project costs less than $2 million and should be done by the end of May. But that's not all. Trump wants to build a huge triumphal arch, like the ones in ancient Rome. He's also renovating the Kennedy Center and putting his name on signs there. The Rose Garden was paved over, and the Oval Office got a gold makeover. Some people love the changes. Others are upset. Neil Flanagan, an architect, says Trump is treating the city "like it's his personal country club." He worries the projects are more about Trump's brand than America's future. With the country's 250th birthday coming up in July, Trump says these projects celebrate American glory. But critics say they're just expensive costumes while other important things, like science, get less money. What do you think — is this a cool upgrade or too much?
why_it_matters: If you ever visit Washington, D.C., the look of the monuments and public spaces can shape what you learn about America's story and who gets to tell it.

background_read: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is part of the National Mall, where historic events like Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech took place.
Triumphal arches were built by ancient Romans to honor emperors and victories; the most famous is the Arch of Constantine in Rome.
The Kennedy Center (opened in 1971) is a major performing arts center named after President John F. Kennedy.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, architect Neil Flanagan, and the public who visits D.C.
WHAT: Trump is redecorating Washington landmarks, including painting the Reflecting Pool blue and proposing a giant triumphal arch
WHERE: Washington, D.C., at places like the Lincoln Memorial, Kennedy Center, and the White House
WHY: Trump enjoys construction and believes these projects celebrate American greatness, but critics say it's more about his personal brand

perspectives.description: They see these changes as patriotic and think the city needs a fresh, grand look to celebrate the country's 250th birthday.
They argue Trump is spending money on expensive decorations while ignoring more important needs like science funding, and that he's treating public property like a private club.
Some people just think it's a matter of taste and that every president has the right to change parts of the White House and nearby landmarks during their term.
